title: The Village Voted for Nobody
layout: One vertical page with five readable panels: a wide opening, the ballot question, a diagonal split debate, the certified count, and a large quiet closing panel.

units.title: The tea
units.purpose: Open with Barkeep and establish that the village is becoming a city.
units.scene: The bright holders room, polished mahogany counter, rounded art-deco windows, and the new Town Hall visible across the square in daylight.
units.action: Barkeep wipes one small circle on the mahogany with the folded cloth, leans toward the reader, and glances toward Town Hall.
units.composition: Wide establishing panel with Barkeep large in the foreground and Town Hall readable through the window; reserve one empty speech balloon and one small caption box

captions: THE VILLAGE WAS BECOMING A REAL CITY.

continuity: Barkeep uses the approved base-cat sheet with no added wardrobe.
The polishing cloth appears exactly once.
Town Hall uses cream stone, muted teal trim, brass details, and clear daylight.

units.title: The question
units.scene: Inside the same bright Town Hall chamber with a cream and teal civic podium, brass ballot fixture, dense resident silhouettes, and one oversized empty mayor's chair.
units.action: Clerk opens the dark teal ballot ledger on the podium and presents one blank ballot strip toward the empty chair.
units.composition: Medium-wide panel with Clerk and podium in the foreground, empty chair as the second focal point, crowd behind; reserve one large empty speech balloon and one narrow civic caption box

dialogue.speaker: clerk
dialogue.text: SHALL THE VILLAGE ELECT A MAYOR?

captions: ELECTED WEEKLY. RECALLABLE. VOICE AND AGENDA. NO COMMAND POWER.

continuity: The mayor's chair remains completely empty.
Clerk uses the approved cream civic vest and no other costume.
The ballot ledger and one blank ballot strip appear exactly once.

units.title: Yes versus No
units.purpose: Show the strongest argument on each side without adding candidates.
units.scene: A diagonal split composition: Barkeep at the holders-room counter on one side and Critic inside Town Hall on the other, both in the same daylight palette.
units.action: Barkeep points at a fixed Yes placard while gripping the polishing cloth; Critic taps the black review slate with the cream pencil and glares toward the empty chair.
units.composition: Diagonal split panel with one character per half and one empty speech balloon per character; keep both silhouettes large and immediately distinct

dialogue.speaker: barkeep
dialogue.text: SOMEONE'S GOTTA TAKE THE HEAT WHEN THE PLUMBING SHITS THE BED.

dialogue.speaker: critic
dialogue.text: WE HAVE A CLERK AND AN OFFICER. WE DO NOT NEED A MASCOT.

continuity: Each character has exactly two arms and two gloved hands.
Barkeep has no added wardrobe; Critic has only the approved heavier eyebrows.
The chair is visible only on Critic's side and remains empty.

units.title: The count
units.purpose: Certify the exact result and turnout.
units.scene: The same Town Hall chamber and podium, with residents leaning into the frame and the empty mayor's chair still visible behind Teller.
units.action: Teller finishes counting on the compact brass abacus, separates the beads into two clean groups, and presents one blank receipt.
units.composition: Energetic medium panel centered on Teller and the abacus; reserve one result board area and one empty speech balloon

dialogue.speaker: teller
dialogue.text: THE VILLAGE REMAINS WITHOUT A MAYOR.

continuity: Teller uses the approved teal accountant visor.
The compact brass abacus and one blank receipt appear exactly once.
The mayor's chair remains empty and the daylight direction does not change.

units.title: Nobody takes office
units.purpose: Land the factual result and Gaspard's dry joke in one quiet image.
units.scene: The same Town Hall chamber in calm morning light, with the untouched empty mayor's chair centered and the working town visible through the windows.
units.action: Gaspard stands at the edge of the empty chair, lowers the closed gallery ledger, holds the round mirror, and looks directly at the reader without smiling.
units.composition: Large quiet closing panel with the empty chair as the primary focal point and Gaspard offset at the edge; reserve one large caption area and one small final speech balloon

dialogue.speaker: gaspard
dialogue.text: FINALLY, A POLITICIAN WHO DOESN'T LIE ABOUT HIS INTENTIONS. BOF.

captions: THE VILLAGE VOTED FOR A VOID IN THE MAYOR'S OFFICE.

continuity: Gaspard uses the approved black beret and cream stained smock.
The round mirror and closed gallery ledger appear exactly once.
No candidate, portrait, crown, sash, or mayor character appears.
